title: cross-sdk-py-ts-go-lightweight-retry-presets-and-streaming-shims
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce lightweight, opinionated retry presets across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; add ergonomic streaming helpers and parity fixes. Minor SDK version bumps and changelog updates.
description:
Motivation: We ship multiple SDKs with slightly divergent retry configuration shapes and streaming ergonomics. Teams repeatedly implement ad-hoc retry wrappers and stream adapters when integrating with Redwood. This PR rolls out a small, lightweight set of retry presets (fast/flexible/strict), a compact backoff builder, and a set of ergonomic stream shims (pullstream sugar + small helpers) implemented in the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The goal is pragmatic parity: same behavior and surface across languages without heavy API churn.

What this PR does (high level): - Introduces three named retry presets (fast, balanced, strict) and a compact builder to compose max_retries, base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, jitter_mode. Presets are opinionated for typical product/PLG use cases. - Adds small streaming helper modules: StreamBuffer (bounded in-memory chunk collector), pullstream adapter utilities (pause/resume hints), and a compact stream-cursor facade for long-lived responses. - Harmonizes config field names (retry -> retry_profile, backoff -> backoff_policy) across SDKs and adds compatibility shims for older callers. - Adds CI-level integration tests exercising cross-language retry behavior with a controlled flaky-auth proxy (local test harness). - Bumps SDK package versions (minor) and updates CHANGELOGs and migration notes.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in Linear ENG-6274) reviewed with SDK leads - [x] Implementations in py/ts/go - [x] Unit tests for backoff math and preset selection - [x] Integration test with flaky auth proxy - [x] Docs + changelog + migration notes - [x] CI green and squash-merge applied

Commits summary: ["feat(sdk): add retry preset builder and presets (py/ts/go)", "feat(sdk): add stream helpers and small pullstream adapters (py/ts/go)", "chore(sdk): normalize config field names and provide compatibility shim", "test(ci): add cross-sdk integration test harness and flaky-proxy", "docs: update changelogs and migration guide", "ci: bump matrix to include new integration job"]

Files / areas changed (high level): - sdks/python/redwood_sdk/retry.py (new preset builder, presets, compatibility layer) - sdks/python/redwood_sdk/stream_helpers.py (StreamBuffer, pullstream adapter) - sdks/python/tests/test_retry_presets.py (unit tests) - sdks/typescript/src/retry/presets.ts (builder + presets) - sdks/typescript/src/stream/helpers.ts (stream shims) - sdks/typescript/test/integration/retry_spec.ts - sdks/go/retry/presets.go (builder + presets) - sdks/go/stream/helpers.go - sdks/go/integration/flaky_proxy_test.go - docs/sdk-migration/retry-presets.md - CHANGELOGs for all three sdks - .github/workflows/sdk-integration.yml (new job)

Key implementation notes: - Presets are intentionally conservative (balanced default yields 3 retries, base_delay_ms=50, max_delay_ms=2000, jitter=full). Strict preset is aggressive about retries but quick to fallback; fast is low-retry low-latency. - Backoff math is deterministic and covered by unit tests; jitter implementations are seeded in tests to avoid flakiness. - The streaming helpers are thin adapters that do not change underlying transport protocols; they only provide ergonomic buffers and suspend/resume hints for consumers. - Compatibility shim: old config keys map to new names with warnings logged once per process to avoid noisy logs for high-throughput services.

Review conversation (high level; chronological): - Jonah Reed (reviewer): "Nice compact surface. Can we avoid logging warnings by default for server-side deployments? Suggest making warning opt-in via env var."\n  - Author (Priya): "Updated: changed warning emission to be opt-in (REDWOOD_SDK_WARN_MIGRATION) and added migration note in docs. Kept a single once-per-process guard in tests to preserve previous behaviour for OSS users by default."\n  - Jonah: "LGTM for the py/ts codepaths. Please add a small comment in the Go shim about runtime setenv limitation."\n  - Marisol Alvarez: "Integration test failed once on CI (auth-flaky proxy); looks like a 1s timing flake in Go test. Can you add a small retry loop in the harness?"\n  - Author: "Added retry loop and extended timeout on the harness. Re-ran CI."\n  - Ethan Chen: "Docs and changelogs look good. One nit: prefer 'retry_profile' in examples to match new naming; fixed comment in TS examples."\n  - Final approvals: Jonah Reed (approved), Marisol Alvarez (approved), Ethan Chen (approved).

CI summary: - .github/workflows/sdk-unit: success - .github/workflows/sdk-lint: success (ts lint autofixed in separate commit) - .github/workflows/sdk-integration (matrix: py/ts/go): first run had one flaky failure (Go flaky_proxy_test), re-run after harness timeout bump passed. Final CI status: pass.

Migration & rollout: - Minor version bumps: python 1.13.0 -> 1.14.0, typescript 2.7.1 -> 2.8.0, go v0.9.8 -> v0.10.0 - Migration notes added documenting new config keys and opt-in migration warnings. We do not consider this a breaking change; defaults are backward-compatible via the compatibility shim. - Recommend SDKs be published after a short staging window; internal infra teams notified via Linear and #sdk-updates Slack channel.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Commit message includes summary and links to Linear ENG-6274. Changelog entries updated in each SDK package and changelog PRs for package registries queued by the release manager.
